summary: Christine Chojnacki is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991 and is attested as a professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 in 2018.

Christine Mollier is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper. She served as a CNRS researcher (1989–1995) and Research Director (attested 2014), and as Numata Visiting Professor at the University of Chicago.

Christmas Humphreys (1901–1983) was an English scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Malvern College and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served as President of The Buddhist Society from circa 1924 to 1983 and taught Alan Watts.

Christoph Anderl is a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned his MA at the University of Vienna (circa 1989–1995) and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo (circa 1997–2004) under Christoph Harbsmeier.

Christoph Cüppers is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (1976–1983) under Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, and Albrecht Wezler, later serving as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute (circa 1993–2013).

Christoph Emmrich specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Heidelberg University by 2004, held an attested post there in 2001, and has served as an assistant professor at the University of Toronto.

Christoph Harbsmeier is a sinologist and linguist who studied at Merton College, Oxford, and Copenhagen. He taught at Universiti Sains Malaysia (1973–1976) before becoming a professor at the University of Oslo in 1980 and an advisory professor at several Chinese universities.

Christoph Kleine is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Bukkyo University and the University of Marburg, he held posts at Marburg and Munich before being appointed professor of religious history at Leipzig University in 2008.

Christoph Theodosius Walther (1699–1741) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After studying theology at the University of Halle in 1720, he served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission from circa 1725 to 1740.

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf (1909–1995) was an anthropologist working in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at Vienna and the LSE, was a professor at Osmania University, and held the Chair of Asian Anthropology at the University of London (1951–1976).
Christophe Jaffrelot is an Indologist who completed his studies at Sciences Po in 1991 under Jean Leca. Around 1991, he assumed posts at Sciences Po and the CNRS.
Christophe Vielle is an Indologist who has served as a professor of Sanskrit at UCLouvain, where his posts are attested in 2009 and 2013.
Christopher Byrne is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McGill University (attested 2015), studying under Grace S. Fong, G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and Robin D. S. Yates.
Christopher D. Emms is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued his doctoral studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke.

Christopher G. Framarin works in philosophy and Indology. He earned an MA in philosophy from the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD from the University of New Mexico, later becoming an associate professor at the University of Calgary.
Christopher Hatchell is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Virginia under the mentorship of David Germano.

Christopher I. Beckwith is a scholar of Tibetology, Central Asian studies, and linguistics. Educated at Ohio State and Indiana University under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, he was appointed professor of Central Eurasian studies at Indiana University in 1982.

Christopher Ives is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He served as assistant professor of religion at the University of Puget Sound (circa 1989–2000) and later became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College.

Christopher Jon Jensen is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University, where he completed his PhD in 2018 under the supervision of James A. Benn.

Christopher Kelley is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his PhD at Columbia University, where he co-founded the Columbia Society for Comparative Philosophy. He has taught at Columbia, The New School, and Brooklyn College.
